reference_findings.fact: Two-point rectangle uses opposite corners; width and height may be entered during placement. The tutorial describes Tab switching numeric fields, repeated rectangles, and Escape ending the tool. Official instructions also specify Enter completing the tool.

Two-point rectangle adds horizontal or vertical constraints to its sides automatically; dragging an undimensioned corner retains orthogonal sides. The tutorial distinguishes fully constrained black geometry from underconstrained blue geometry.

D activates Sketch Dimension. Select a line or two points, position and click the canvas annotation, then enter a value and accept with Enter. The dimension tool remains active for another dimension until Escape.
Double-click a placed dimension to edit its numeric value; Enter accepts. Dimension annotations can be repositioned in the canvas.

Driving dimensions control geometry. Driven dimensions update from geometry and display in parentheses. The tutorial describes an overconstraint warning offering a driven dimension; official docs describe driving as the default unless overconstrained.

Choosing a sketch plane exposes the Sketch Palette at the right in the tutorial. It discusses grid, snapping, points, constraints and profile visibility. Instructor-specific toggles are not established defaults.
L is Line, R is two-point Rectangle and D is Sketch Dimension.

comparison.current: New rectangles atomically add four orientation constraints with fresh stable IDs to their four new shared-endpoint lines. The real-app case inspected those constraints, fixed one corner, drove width/height, checked zero DOF, edited width and preserved authored state through undo and native save/reopen. Existing files retain their authored constraints.
comparison.recommendation: Retain this verified automatic rectangle behavior; arbitrary line inference remains a separate compatibility task.
comparison.verification: Create an unanchored rectangle, inspect four orientation constraints, edit width and verify orthogonal sides survive solve, undo and save/reopen.

comparison.current: D selects dimension mode; geometry selection and palette controls add dimensions. The source now renders numeric labels, including parenthesized driven values, but labels have fixed offsets and no canvas placement or double-click editor.
comparison.recommendation: Keep this first equation slice explicitly partial. Add shared dimension placement/accept/cancel state, canvas annotation picking and inline numeric entry as a bounded familiarity follow-up.
comparison.verification: Physical D, line selection, placement click, numeric Enter, second dimension, Escape; then double-click/edit the annotation. Inspect identical shared API/session state and one intended commit.

comparison.current: Explicit driving checkbox and driven measurements exist; solver errors reject inconsistent input. No documented-equivalent overconstraint-to-driven prompt is implemented.
comparison.recommendation: Offer explicit convert-to-driven on a rejected redundant driving dimension, preserving usable draft and dimensions; do not silently accept a failed solve.
comparison.verification: Attempt a dependent dimension, choose driven, inspect unchanged geometry and parenthesized updated measurement.

comparison.current: Click-click rectangle placement and Escape-to-select are implemented; exact coordinates are in the dock palette. Inline width/height with Tab and Enter tool completion remain absent.
comparison.recommendation: Implement inline entry and tool completion through the same draft commands after dimension placement is usable.
comparison.verification: Type width, Tab, height, place; Escape or Enter stops the drawing tool while retaining the sketch draft.

comparison.current: Developing source colors the entire draft based on total DOF, displays points/selection and dimension text. Per-entity constraint badges and independent visibility switches remain incomplete.
comparison.recommendation: Track badges, selective visibility and per-entity constraint state without claiming exact theme/color parity from older tutorials.
comparison.verification: Capture comparable constrained/unconstrained and selected states, recording app size/scale/theme and the chosen public reference age.
